newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat seasonally out of favor, sharpens fall.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat seasonally out of favor, sharpens fall.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil sharpened its losses late session Monday afternoon as the tail end of winter continued to produce relatively mild temperatures.
Technical selling throughout the oil complex was also a contributor, traders said.

At 1440 EST, March heating oil was off 2.00 cents a gallon at 55.85 cents, and March gasoline was off 1.27 cents at 60.55 cents a gallon. The March/April spread had fallen to 0.75 cent from 1.23 cents Friday.
"We may get close to contango in heat as supply is there but the weather isn't," said a dealer.

Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp, based in Lexington, Mass., forecasted that temperatures would moderate to above normal this week in the northeastern United States just as it did last week. The region has the highest concentration of heating oil demand in the world.

Distillate stocks, including heating oil, usually show declines this time of year since refiners have already started to shift production away from heating oil to make gasoline. However, traders expect slack demand to temper the stock decline in this week's oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute to be released Tuesday.
For the week ended February 14, heating oil supplies were about even with year ago in the Northeast and 1.3 million barrels above a year ago for all the U.S. regions combined.
March crude was 72 cents off at $20.68 a barrel. The sell-off in prompt crude accelerated after April crude broke its simple 200-day moving average of $20.99 Monday morning.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
